topics.title: Your First Turn
topics.subtitle: No idea what to do? Start here! Each step has its own category in this Help window. You can also drag this Help window around.

items.heading: Look around
items.text: Use the map view buttons to see terrain, countries, and resources. See Map & Controls.

items.heading: Start research
items.text: Open R&D on the left bar and start a few technologies. See Research.

items.heading: Build something
items.text: Click one of your provinces and press Production to queue buildings or units. See Production.

items.heading: Move units
items.text: In Units view, left-click a unit stack, then right-click a tile to send it there. See Units & Orders.

items.heading: End the turn
items.text: Press Next Turn. Every country's orders resolve at the same time.

topics.title: Reading the Screen
topics.subtitle: Where to find your country's situation at a glance.

items.heading: Resources
items.text: The bottom bar shows your Manpower, Materials, and Fuel. The number in brackets is how much each one changes next turn.

items.heading: Date
items.text: The date is shown in the bottom bar. Each turn moves it forward.

items.heading: Country name
items.text: The top bar names your country, or the owner of the tile you selected.

items.heading: Left bar
items.text: Opens your country's screens: Identity, Economy, R&D, Mail, Save, Settings, Music, Faction, Claims, Puppets, Automation, and Politics.

items.heading: Unit events
items.text: The yellow mail button beside the resource bar lists what happened to your units last turn.

topics.title: Ending a Turn
topics.subtitle: Orders take effect when the turn ends, not when you give them.

items.heading: Next Turn
items.text: Press Next Turn in the bottom bar when your orders are ready. In real-time multiplayer the button reads Submit Turn, and in tournaments it reads Export Turn.

items.heading: What happens
items.text: Unit orders such as conversions, disbanding, repairs, and upgrades advance first. Then production, air missions, bombardment, movement, and battles resolve. Income and research come last.

items.heading: Save
items.text: Press Save on the left bar and choose a name. Load the game again from Load Game in the main menu.

topics.title: Map Navigation
topics.subtitle: Your country is centered automatically when a game opens or after you choose it. If you're familiar with how HOI4 map controls work, then the default map controls for GD5 should be very easy to understand.

items.heading: LEFT MOUSE
lines: Click a unit stack to select it; Shift-click adds more.
Drag in Units view to box-select units.

items.heading: MIDDLE MOUSE
lines: Hold and drag to pan the map.
Scroll up or down to zoom in or out.

items.heading: RIGHT MOUSE
lines: Drag to pan the map outside Orders.
Right-click moves selected units; Shift queues a waypoint.

blocks.heading: ARROW KEYS
blocks.text: Use the arrow keys to pan the map. You can customize these in Settings > Keybinds.
Customize mouse gestures in Settings > Mouse Settings.

topics.title: Map UI
topics.subtitle: These buttons are important! Located on the bottom left of the screen, they edit the appearance of the map, giving you the information you need to play effectively.

items.heading: Terrain
items.text: Shows the terrain map.

items.heading: Political
items.text: Shows the actual countries on the map.

items.heading: Relations
items.text: Shows diplomatic relations.

items.heading: Cores
items.text: Shows the territory each country has cores on.

items.heading: Factions
items.text: Shows factions.

items.heading: Resources
items.text: Shows province resources.

items.heading: Blank
items.text: Hides the secondary map overlay.

items.heading: Units
items.text: Shows unit stacks and their commands.

items.heading: Economy
items.text: Shows economic map information.

items.heading: Names
items.text: Shows or hides country names.

blocks.text: In Units view you will see 4 colored buttons in the bottom left corner, which are Naval [icon:naval:24], Land [icon:land:24], Air [icon:air:24], and All [icon:all:24]. These filter your view of the map so you only see units that belong in that category. Click Hide above the buttons to slide the strip down. Click Show to slide it up again. Your selected filter stays active. Switching away from Units view slides the strip closed. The Hide/Show button stays visible, disabled, and without text. Returning opens the strip unless you used Hide. All is selected whenever a game opens.

topics.title: Moving Units
topics.subtitle: Units follow the shortest path they are allowed to take.

items.heading: Select
items.text: In Units view, left-click a unit stack. Shift-click adds more stacks, and dragging draws a selection box. Orders opens for the selected units.

items.heading: Move
items.text: Right-click a tile to send the selected units there. Hold Shift while right-clicking to add a waypoint.

items.heading: Speed
items.text: A unit's speed is how many tiles it can move each turn. Longer moves continue over the next turns.

items.heading: Where land units can go
items.text: Your land, land of your faction members, land where you have military access, unclaimed land, and land of countries you are at war with.

items.heading: Change orders
items.text: A new move order replaces the old one. Clear ALL Orders in Orders cancels the orders of the units shown there.

topics.title: Unit Commands
topics.subtitle: Each unit row in Orders has command buttons. Hover over a button to see what it does, or why it is unavailable.

items.heading: Convert
items.text: Turns a land unit on the coast into a Convoy, or a ship into a Truck. See Crossing Water.

items.heading: Repair
items.text: Restores a damaged unit. The unit needs a factory on its tile and cannot be in a battle.

items.heading: Upgrade
items.text: Replaces the unit with a newer researched model. The unit needs a factory on its tile and cannot be in a battle.

items.heading: Disband
items.text: Removes the unit after one turn and refunds its cost.

items.heading: Rename and Bombard
items.text: Rename gives the unit its own name. Units with bombardment, such as artillery, can fire at a target tile.

items.heading: Several units
items.text: With more than one unit selected, the Disband, Repair, and Upgrade buttons at the top of Orders apply to all of them.

topics.title: Crossing Water
topics.subtitle: Land units need to become a Convoy before they can cross the sea.

items.heading: Board a convoy
items.text: On a coastal tile, press Convert on a land unit. When the conversion finishes, the unit is a Convoy that can move onto water.

items.heading: Land again
items.text: Move the Convoy onto a land tile, then press Convert to turn it back into the land unit. A Convoy caught in a battle on land unloads by itself.

items.heading: Ships over land
items.text: With Trucks research, a ship on a coastal tile can convert into a Truck and travel over land. Convert it back on a coast.

items.heading: Ships and the coast
items.text: Ships can dock in friendly coastal tiles, but they cannot take land. Warships caught in a battle on land are destroyed.

items.heading: Timing
items.text: A conversion takes time and cannot start during a battle. Press Convert again to cancel it.

topics.title: Armies
topics.subtitle: Learn how to create, organize, and command armies, including target areas.

items.heading: Select units
items.text: Left-click stacks or drag in Units view. In Orders, right-click a unit row to add or remove it without changing the other selected units.

items.heading: Unassigned
items.text: Select units outside armies with this first, dark grey card. It has no emblem or editing controls. It hides when all units are assigned or Settings > Show Unassigned is OFF. Unassigned units keep their map icons.

items.heading: Create an army
items.text: In Orders, click + Create Army in the Army tray. (Located on the right side of the screen)

items.heading: Personalize
items.text: Click a card to select the units in said army. Pressing the E button edits its name and emblem.

items.heading: Target areas
items.text: Press T on an army card, select its target tiles, and confirm. The army fills uncovered tiles first, then balances its units. Units that have no orders given will automatically be ordered to fill in the target area next turn.

items.heading: Need to Assign more units?
items.text: With units selected, right-click an army card.

topics.title: Battles
topics.subtitle: A battle starts when units of countries at war share a tile.

items.heading: Front and reserve
items.text: Each turn, the front units of both sides fight. Terrain decides how many units fit in the front. The rest wait in reserve, take no damage, and recover morale.

items.heading: Leaving a battle
items.text: Units fighting in a battle stop their moves. They can only leave by one tile per turn, into land that is not hostile.

items.heading: Find battles
items.text: In Units view, battles show as bubbles. Click a bubble to open Orders for that tile.

items.heading: Manage Battle
items.text: In Orders, Manage Battle lets you choose which enemy each unit faces and which units wait in reserve. Without units there, the button reads View Battle.

items.heading: Production pauses
items.text: Buildings and units queued in a province stop progressing while a battle is fought there.

topics.title: Taking Land
topics.subtitle: Land units take a tile by standing in it after its defenders are gone.

items.heading: Capture
items.text: Move a land unit into unclaimed land, or into land of a country you are at war with. The tile becomes yours at the end of the turn once no defenders are left.

items.heading: Ships and aircraft
items.text: Ships and aircraft cannot take land.

items.heading: Forts
items.text: A Fort gives the defenders of its tile a bonus. Bombardment can damage a fort.

items.heading: Cores
items.text: Land you do not have a core on gives much less income. Use Core Territory in Production to add your core.

topics.title: Aircraft
topics.subtitle: Green outlines represent an aircraft's movement range, yellow ones represent their mission range.

items.heading: Missions
items.text: Choose Move, Strike, Transport, Air Drop, or defense from the mission button. Click a target for a flight mission. No mission cancels the order. Esc cancels target selection.

items.heading: Strike / defend
items.text: Click enemy territory or visible enemy units while giving movement orders to strike, including enemies on your land. Aircraft attack without landing. Defenders can fire back, and surviving aircraft return with losses. Enemy aircraft on defense missions may intercept several missions.

items.heading: Reposition
items.text: With Move or Strike active, another order click changes the target but keeps the mission type. Use the mission selector to switch missions. Idle planes show green relocation range (except V1 and V2); defense and strikes show yellow.

items.heading: V1 / V2
items.text: V1 and V2 air units die when their strike completes, and they relocate on land at ground speed, unlike other planes.

items.heading: Aircraft details
items.text: Research shows current range and abilities. Unavailable missions are disabled. Use range outlines to choose targets. Air missions have no aircraft limit; larger allied stacks reduce attack efficiency.

items.heading: Other Information
items.text: Tanks cannot damage aircraft in flight. Aircraft cannot land on enemy or unclaimed land. Aircraft caught in ground combat die immediately. Aircraft carriers cannot hold aircraft (yet).

topics.title: Air transport
topics.subtitle: Carry ground units between accessible land tiles, or air drop them into enemy territory.

items.heading: Load cargo
items.text: Choose Transport, then select your ground units on the plane's tile. Transports also offer Move and Air Drop.

items.heading: Eligible units
items.text: Ships and other planes cannot be cargo. A ship packed into a Truck can be loaded. Research details show each transport's current capacity and range. Cancel a unit's paid order before loading it.

items.heading: Fly with cargo
items.text: Loaded units leave the map and stay aboard the plane. Use Move to fly with cargo. The Air Transport icon stays during Move and order cancellation. An active Air Drop order uses the Air Drop icon.

items.heading: Air Drop
items.text: Choose Air Drop in the cargo picker, then enemy land. Idle loaded planes also drop when ordered there. Range is half Move range. Patrols intercept before the drop. Surviving planes return to base. During recovery, dropped units can capture land and destroy grounded enemy aircraft. They cannot move, take commands, or deal normal combat damage. Orders shows the turns remaining.

items.heading: Cargo damage
items.text: Cargo loses the same fraction of its current health as the plane. For example, losing half the plane's remaining health also removes half each carried unit's remaining health. If the plane is destroyed, its cargo is destroyed too.

items.heading: Release cargo
items.text: Choose Transport again and select Release for a carried unit. It appears on the plane's tile and can move immediately. Loading and releasing it in the same turn does not consume its movement. Load and release on land outside combat.

topics.title: The Production Screen
topics.subtitle: Click one of your provinces, then press Production in the province menu.

items.heading: Rows
items.text: The list has administrative actions, buildings, and units. Each row shows the cost, the build time, and what the row produces.

items.heading: Grey buttons
items.text: A grey button cannot be used in this province yet. Building... means one building of that type is already in progress.

items.heading: Queues
items.text: The Buildings and Units panels list what this province is producing. See Queues and Refunds.

items.heading: Stockpiles
items.text: The bar at the bottom of the screen shows the resources you have.

topics.title: Buildings
topics.subtitle: A province holds one building of each type. Building the next level replaces the current one.

items.heading: Factory
items.text: Produces resources, mainly materials. A province needs a factory to recruit most units and to repair or upgrade them.

items.heading: Recruitment Building
items.text: Produces manpower. It needs a Basic Factory in the province first.

items.heading: Fort
items.text: Gives the defenders of the province a bonus in battle.

items.heading: Levels
items.text: Each row offers the next level of that building. Some levels appear only after research.

items.heading: Cores
items.text: Core Territory adds your core to the province over a few turns, which raises its income. Remove Cores removes foreign cores, needs a garrison, and starts a rebellion.

topics.title: Recruiting Units
topics.subtitle: The unit sections list the newest unit of each type you have researched.

items.heading: Queue a unit
items.text: Click a unit button to pay for the unit and add it to the province's unit queue.

items.heading: Factories
items.text: Most units need a finished factory in the province. Their buttons stay grey until the province has one.

items.heading: Variants
items.text: Small toggles such as Mot, Mec, IFV, and Hvy switch a row to that variant once you have researched it.

items.heading: Custom
items.text: The Custom section lets you choose older researched units to build.

items.heading: Deployment
items.text: The new unit appears in the province when its build time is over.

topics.title: Queues and Refunds
topics.subtitle: You pay the full cost when you place an order.

items.heading: Two queues
items.text: Each province has a building queue and a unit queue. Only the first item in each queue makes progress each turn.

items.heading: Cancel
items.text: Click an entry in the Buildings or Units panel to cancel it. You get back what you paid.

items.heading: Battles
items.text: Queues stop progressing while a battle is fought in the province.

items.heading: Not enough resources
items.text: An order you cannot afford is refused, and nothing is charged.

topics.title: Resources
topics.subtitle: Your country uses three resources: Manpower, Materials, and Fuel.

items.heading: Manpower
items.text: Units cost manpower to recruit and to keep.

items.heading: Materials
items.text: Buildings and units cost materials.

items.heading: Fuel
items.text: Many vehicles, ships, and aircraft cost fuel.

items.heading: Upkeep
items.text: Every unit costs part of its price each turn. The number in brackets on the resource bar is your income minus upkeep.

items.heading: Running low
items.text: A stockpile cannot drop below zero, but you cannot place new orders without enough resources.

topics.title: Income
topics.subtitle: Income is added at the end of every turn.

items.heading: Land
items.text: Every tile you own adds income. Tiles you have a core on give more than tiles you do not.

items.heading: Natural resources
items.text: Iron adds materials, Coal and Oil add fuel, and Wheat adds manpower. The Resources map view shows where they are.

items.heading: Buildings
items.text: Factories and Recruitment Buildings add income from their province.

items.heading: Research and policies
items.text: Some technologies and Politics policies raise income.

topics.title: The Economy Tab
topics.subtitle: Open Economy on the left bar to see where your income comes from.

items.heading: Breakdown
items.text: Each resource is split into its sources and costs, so you can see what each one adds.

items.heading: Conscription
items.text: The Conscription (Keep Manpower %) slider sets how much manpower you keep. The rest becomes materials.

items.heading: Fuel conversion
items.text: The Convert % Mats to Fuel slider turns part of your materials into fuel. It needs Fuel Refining research.

items.heading: Expenses
items.text: Expenses lists the upkeep of your units.

topics.title: Researching Technology
topics.subtitle: Open R&D on the left bar.

items.heading: Choose a category
items.text: Pick a category at the top. Its technologies are placed on a timeline by year.

items.heading: Start
items.text: Click a technology to see its details and what it unlocks, then press Start Research.

items.heading: Slots
items.text: You can research only a few technologies at once. Slots Full means every slot is in use.

items.heading: Pause
items.text: Pause stops a project and keeps its progress.

items.heading: Missing Reqs
items.text: Research the required technologies first.

items.heading: Researching early
items.text: A technology researched before its year takes longer. The further ahead it is, the slower it goes.

topics.title: What Research Unlocks
topics.subtitle: Finished research changes what you can build and earn.

items.heading: Units
items.text: New units appear in Production once you research them.

items.heading: Upgrades
items.text: Units you already have can upgrade to newer models from Orders.

items.heading: Buildings
items.text: Some building levels need research before they appear in Production.

items.heading: Economy
items.text: Technologies such as General Recruitment, Resource Refining, Fuel Refining, and Bergius Process add income or new options.

topics.title: Other Countries
topics.subtitle: Reach other countries through the Mail tab or directly from their territory on the map.

items.heading: Country summary
items.text: Click the top-left flag for a read-only summary. Select another country's tile to inspect that country.

items.heading: Mail
items.text: Open the Mail tab (located to the left) to read, reply to, or start conversations.

items.heading: Country actions
items.text: Click another country's tile to see available diplomatic actions you can take against them.

topics.title: War and Peace
topics.subtitle: Select another country's tile to see what you can do with that country.

items.heading: Declare war
items.text: Press Declare War. While you are at war with that country, the same button offers Ceasefire / Peace.

items.heading: Military access
items.text: Request Mil. Access to move units through another country's land without a war.

items.heading: Factions
items.text: Faction members are friendly, and their units can enter each other's land. Use Create Faction, Invite to Faction, or Req. Join Faction.

items.heading: Shared wars
items.text: Within a faction, Join Wars joins that member's wars, and Call to Arms asks that member to join yours.

topics.title: Mail and Timing
topics.subtitle: Diplomacy happens between turns, not instantly.

items.heading: Sending
items.text: Messages, requests, and declarations are queued. They are sent when the turn ends.

items.heading: Replies
items.text: The other country receives them next turn, and can answer only then.

items.heading: Requests
items.text: In Mail, a request has Accept, Decline, and View buttons. View opens the terms of a trade or peace treaty.

items.heading: Queued replies
items.text: A queued reply can be undone until the turn ends.
